inventory.name: flex-wrap: balance — the new `balance` keyword on the existing flex-wrap property, making a multi-line flex container balance its flex lines

syntax.rationale: The declaration surface, in semantic <code> inside the property-value table: the property `flex-wrap`, the new value `balance`, the unchanged existing values `nowrap`/`wrap`/`wrap-reverse`, and the axis row. GAP FLAGGED, NOT PAPERED OVER: the table lists the keywords but not the spec grammar `nowrap | [ wrap | wrap-reverse ] || balance`, so a reader cannot derive from this page that `balance` combines with `wrap` or `wrap-reverse`, that the grammar does not admit `nowrap balance`, or that a bare `balance` behaves as if `wrap` had been specified (css-flexbox-2 §5.2). Writing that grammar is prose work outside this unit's minimum edit; recorded in notes and in the report.

inputs.rationale: The inputs to this surface are declarative, and the table enumerates them: the keyword the author writes (`balance`, against the unchanged `nowrap`/`wrap`/`wrap-reverse`) and the container it is written on (the Direction row's scope note). There is no script-facing parameter list, so the value keyword set plus the element scope is the whole input surface.

outputs.rationale: The output is a rendering change, stated in #why-it-exists (line breaks adjusted so items spread evenly instead of leaving a short last line, without switching to display: grid) and shown in #live-demo by a rendered balance/wrap pair. DIVERGENCE REPORTED, NOT FIXED: the page says the algorithm makes 'the number of items per line ... as equal as possible', while css-flexbox-2 §9.7 minimises the sum of the squared error where a line's error is its SIZE (the sum of the items' outer hypothetical main sizes, floored at 0) minus the container's inner main size, breaking ties toward more items on the earlier lines — the two readings coincide only when the items are equal-sized.

errors.rationale: A keyword added to an existing CSS property has no exception, error-code or rejection surface: there is no call to fail, so nothing throws, and the page documents no error path. The only failure mode is availability — a browser without the value does not apply the declaration — which #browser-support records as version support and #at-a-glance as a flag-gated developer trial. GAP FLAGGED: the page does not state the dropped-declaration fallback itself, although the ChromeStatus record's activation_risks field describes the feature as one that 'gracefully degrades if not supported'; see notes.

context.rationale: Exposure context is the at-a-glance table: in Chrome 149 the value sits behind the developer-trial flag chrome://flags/#enable-experimental-web-platform-features and is enabled by default in Chrome 150, with Firefox and Safari recorded as No signal and the spec plus the ChromeStatus record linked. The element-level scope (flex containers, and the page's row-axis note) is carried by #the-property-value.

lifecycle.rationale: A declarative value has no runtime lifecycle: nothing is constructed, registered, awaited or torn down, and its effect is recomputed at each style and layout pass rather than moving through states of its own. The only transitions the page documents are release-availability ones (developer trial in 149 to enabled by default in 150), which are the context dimension above, not a lifecycle of the value.

examples.rationale: #live-demo carries two rendered containers (balance vs. wrap, same seven items) plus a semantic <pre><code> `.tags` rule using `flex-wrap: balance`, and the sibling recipes section adds two further <pre><code> rules; recipes is not anchored by this contract because its <h2> fragment stops at its first <h3>. The bare `flex-wrap: balance` the examples use is valid per css-flexbox-2 §5.2, which states that a bare balance behaves as if wrap had been specified.

compatibility.rationale: Tabular support: Chrome 149, Edge 149 (Chromium), Firefox No signal, Safari No signal. Verified against the record on 2026-10-07: DevTrial stage desktop_first/android_first 149 and Ship stage desktop_first/android_first 150, ff_views 5 and safari_views 5 = 'No signal'. UNSOURCED CELL REPORTED, NOT ADJUDICATED: the record carries no Edge-specific field, so 'Edge 149 (Chromium)' is an inference from Chromium parity rather than a value in the cited source.

securityPrivacy.rationale: The value exposes no data and grants no capability: it redistributes items that are already in the layout across flex lines, adding no script-visible state, storage, permission, network or cross-origin surface, and #why-it-exists describes only that visual redistribution. Both cited sources say the same from their own side, fetched 2026-10-07: css-flexbox-2's Privacy Considerations and Security Considerations sections read 'No new privacy considerations have been reported on this specification' and 'No new security considerations have been reported on this specification', and ChromeStatus record 4547107962486784 carries security_review_status 'Not applicable', privacy_review_status 'Not applicable' and security_risks 'None.'.

notes: CAMPAIGN B3 UNIT (gendn-g8o), minimum edit + contract. WHAT CHANGED ON THE PAGE: five ids, each on the <h2> element (fragmentAfterId() slices to the next <h1-3>, so an id on a section or on an <h2> that opens with an <h3> would resolve to an empty fragment) — #at-a-glance (context, lifecycle), #why-it-exists (outputs, securityPrivacy), #the-property-value (syntax, inputs, errors), #live-demo (examples), #browser-support (compatibility). The recipes <h2> was deliberately NOT given an id: its fragment stops at its first <h3> and no selector needs it. Two unlinked citation labels were resolved per AGENTS.md:91,103, each named source wrapped in its own <a target="_blank" rel="noopener">: 'chromestatus summary' (why-it-exists) and 'chromestatus browser views' (browser-support), both to https://chromestatus.com/feature/4547107962486784 (curl 200). The third span (the-property-value) already linked CSS Flexbox Level 2. No prose, structure, example code or styling was changed, and the pre-existing bare spec-root href was left as it is. SOURCES RE-FETCHED, NOT ASSUMED (2026-10-07, all curl 200): css-flexbox-2 §5.2 does define this feature — propdef flex-wrap, Value `nowrap | [ wrap | wrap-reverse ] || balance`, Initial nowrap, Applies to flex containers, Computed value specified keyword, Animation type discrete, with the `balance` valdef reading 'The flex container is multi-line, and attempts to balance the lengths of the flex lines to be as similar as possible ... If neither are specified, it behaves as if wrap was specified'; the ChromeStatus record's spec_link is the same URL, its name is 'flex-wrap:balance', its summary matches the page's lede, flag_name is 'experimental-web-platform-features' (the page's flag claim), DevTrial desktop/android 149 (the page's 'developer trial in 149') and Ship desktop/android 150 (the page's 'ships by default in Chrome 150') — those four page claims AGREE with the record. DIVERGENCES FOUND, BOTH SIDES NAMED, NEITHER ADJUDICATED, NONE FIXED (the implementer owns any disclosure sentence and its pin): (1) DIRECTION — the page's #the-property-value row reads 'Rows only (same as flex-wrap: wrap)', while css-flexbox-2 §5.2 says 'Applies to: flex containers' with no direction restriction (flex-wrap wraps along the main axis, so a column container wraps too) and §6.1 explicitly reasons about 'a column flexbox, with unlimited available height' under balance; the same page row's second sentence ('balance applies to line lengths') matches the spec. (2) WHAT IS BALANCED — the page's #why-it-exists says 'the number of items per line is as equal as possible', while §9.7 'Balancing Flex Items' divides items into contiguous sequences that minimise the sum of the squared error, error being the line SIZE (sum of the items' outer hypothetical main sizes, floored at 0) minus the container's inner main size, with ties resolved toward more items on the earlier line; §6 says a balanced flex container 'carefully chooses its linebreaks to make the line lengths as similar as possible'. Item-count and line-length balancing differ whenever the items are not equal-sized. (3) UNSOURCED COMPAT CELL — the page's #browser-support table asserts 'Edge 149 (Chromium)'; the cited record has no Edge field (desktop_first/android_first 149 for DevTrial, 150 for Ship), so that cell is Chromium-parity inference, not a value in the source. (4) PAGE-INTERNAL TENSION, reported with the above: 'Rows only' and 'balance applies to line lengths' sit in the same row, and 'number of items per line' (#why-it-exists) sits against 'line lengths' (#the-property-value) — the spec sides with the line-length phrasing. SUFFICIENCY GAPS FLAGGED HONESTLY, all of them prose work outside this unit's minimum edit: the page never states the value grammar's combinability (`wrap balance` / `wrap-reverse balance`, and that `nowrap balance` is excluded), the bare-`balance`-behaves-as-`wrap` rule, the computed value (specified keyword) or the animation type (discrete); it does not mention §6.1's companion `flex-line-count` property that sets the minimum line count a balance flexbox creates; and it does not state the unsupported-value fallback even though the record's activation_risks field calls graceful degradation the feature's adoption story — which is why errors is this contract's weakest dimension (lifecycle is not-applicable for a separate reason: a declarative value has no runtime state machine). SOURCES PRESENT IN THE RECORD BUT NOT CITED BY THE PAGE (all curl 200 on 2026-10-07; the page names none of them, so the citation ratchet does not require them, and adding them would exceed this unit's edit): Intent to Prototype https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/d/msgid/blink-dev/67eae2d6.170a0220.8108a.099e.GAE%40google.com, Intent to Ship https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/d/msgid/blink-dev/6a171d4a.a860e6c2.3bc0d5.024d.GAE%40google.com, explainer https://github.com/bfgeek/flex-wrap-balance, Chromium bug https://issues.chromium.org/issues/416755656, WPT results https://wpt.fyi/results/css/css-flexbox/balance, initial public proposal https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/3070, TAG review https://github.com/w3ctag/design-reviews/issues/1227.
